f.statement: An applicant for parallel importation must provide an undertaking that it will ensure the continued safety, efficacy and quality of the medicine.

f.title: Include warnings, interactions and side effects in the professional information
f.statement: Professional information for medicines for human use shall contain, among other particulars, contraindications, warnings and special precautions, interactions, human reproduction, side effects, and known symptoms of overdosage and their treatment.
f.clause: Regulation 11 Professional information for medicines for human use
f.legal_basis: General Regulations 2017 (GN 859, Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965), reg. 11(2)

f.title: Include side effects and the general side-effect statement in the patient information leaflet
f.statement: The patient information leaflet shall include side effects with the statement: "Not all side effects reported for this medicine are included in this leaflet. Should your general health worsen or if you experience any untoward effects while taking this medicine, please consult your health care provider for advice", and overdose instructions.

f.title: Submit a DSUR annually and the final safety report within 30 days of trial end
f.statement: The person authorised to conduct a clinical trial shall submit a development safety update report annually and the final safety report 30 days after completion or termination of the clinical trial.
f.legal_basis: General Regulations 2017 (GN 859, Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965), reg. 30(6)(b)

f.title: Principal investigator informs the Authority of suspected adverse events and safety concerns
f.statement: The principal investigator shall inform the Authority of any suspected adverse events or safety concerns occurring as a result of the use of any medicine during the conduct of a clinical trial.
f.legal_basis: General Regulations 2017 (GN 859, Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965), reg. 30(7)

f.title: Inform SAHPRA of quality, safety or effectiveness concerns, ADRs and risk management activities
f.statement: Applicants for registration, holders of a certificate of registration and holders of a section 22C(1)(b) licence must inform the Authority, in the manner and time frame it determines, of any new or existing quality, safety or effectiveness concerns related to any medicine or Scheduled substance, including adverse drug reactions, and of associated risk management activities. This also applies to unregistered medicines sold or used under sections 14(3), 14(4), 15C, 21 and 36 of the Act.

f.statement: Applicants, certificate holders and section 22C(1)(b) licence holders must maintain or have access to records of the reports and case reports of quality, safety and effectiveness concerns and ADRs.

f.title: Conduct and submit a critical safety analysis when requested
f.statement: Whenever requested by the Authority, the applicant or holder must conduct a concise critical analysis of the safety, quality or effectiveness of the medicine or Scheduled substance and submit the results within the specified time frame.
f.legal_basis: General Regulations 2017 (GN 859, Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965), reg. 40(4)(a)

f.title: Submit case reports, usage figures and PSURs if the Authority finds the medicine may not be safe
f.statement: Where, after receiving the analysis, the Authority determines the medicine or Scheduled substance may not be safe to use, the applicant or holder must, if required, submit case reports of all adverse events or suspected or actual ADRs, usage figures where applicable, periodic safety update reports and performance studies, and any other data requested.

f.statement: The applicant or holder must keep and maintain, or have access to, records of the adverse event data in respect of its medicines or Scheduled substances.

f.title: Contravening the product information, leaflet and clinical trial regulations is an offence
f.statement: Any person who fails to comply with, contravenes or furnishes incorrect information in respect of, among others, regulation 11 (professional information), regulation 12 (patient information leaflet), regulation 29 (sale of unregistered medicine) or regulation 30 (conduct of clinical trials) is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine or imprisonment not exceeding 10 years.
